title: A Powerful Weapon
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Nature of the Sword
subpoints: The gladius was a short Roman sword for close-quarter combat.
This indicates the spiritual war is personal, messy, and costly.
Christians must recognize they are in a real war against Satan, not in a neutral world.

outline.title: The Source of Power
subpoints: The Bible is powerful because it is the inspired Word of God.
It is inerrant and free from error.
It serves as a weapon that destroys evil and builds up good.

outline.title: Sufficiency for Life
subpoints: Scripture is sufficient to equip believers for every good work.
It qualifies Christians for all aspects of life, not just major decisions.
The 'man of God' is complete and thoroughly equipped by the Word.

outline.title: The Functions of Scripture
subpoints: Doctrine: Teaching what to believe about God and what He requires of us.
Reproof: Providing evidence and warning to identify what needs to change.
The Bible reveals the knowledge of God and ourselves, which constitutes true wisdom.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro examines the final piece of the armor of God: the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God. Drawing on the historical context of the Roman gladius, the pastor explains that this weapon signifies a close, personal, and costly spiritual war against Satan, countering the modern tendency to view the world as neutral. The Bible is presented as a weapon infinitely more powerful than any earthly arsenal because it is the inspired, inerrant Word of God, capable of both destroying evil and building up righteousness.

The message emphasizes the sufficiency of Scripture, citing 2 Timothy 3:16-17 to demonstrate that the Bible equips believers for every good work and every aspect of daily life. It is argued that there is no need to seek wisdom outside of Scripture, as it is complete for knowing God and oneself. The sermon details how the Word functions through doctrine, teaching believers what to believe about God and what He requires of them, and through reproof, providing the necessary evidence and correction to identify and change sinful behaviors. Ultimately, the Word of God is portrayed as the essential tool for spiritual victory and holistic Christian living.
